# OPEN BLOCKERS — ARKALI GENESIS v2

**As of:** Phase 0 candidate

## Internal blockers

**Status is declared, never inferred.** Each finding's state comes only from its
`Status` cell. Free text in any other column may contain OPEN, CLOSED, HIGH,
`ark_req_ids_closed` or any other token without effect (F-0025).

| F-0033 | **Alembic's autogenerate target held one table out of seven.** `alembic/env.py` set `target_metadata = PersistenceBase.metadata` after importing only the base. That object is populated by the *import side effect* of the modules declaring mapped classes, so the migration tool's picture of the schema was whatever happened to be imported - one table. Autogenerate does not under-report a table it cannot see; it proposes DROPping it. The same import dependency made `test_migrated_schema_matches_the_orm_metadata` order-sensitive: it passed under `pytest -q` and failed under `pytest tests/persistence -q`. Latent since Phase 5 and made visible by Phase 6 adding two contexts' tables. MEDIUM: no migration in the chain was autogenerated, all four are hand-written, and the comparison control failed in the **detecting** direction, so no defective schema was ever admitted and no accepted phase is invalidated | MEDIUM | CLOSED | kernel.persistence | resolved: `env.py` declares `MAPPED_RECORD_MODULES` and imports each, at the migration composition root (outside `backend/arkali`, so no layer direction is crossed - the kernel cannot import rank 1 and rank 2 contexts). Three new controls in `TestAutogenerateTargetIsComplete` derive the mapped-module set from the source tree by AST and fail if `env.py` omits one, declares one that maps nothing, or declares one without importing it; the schema comparison now loads the derived set first, so its verdict no longer depends on collection order. Both mutations - dropping a module from the list, and declaring it without importing it - were proven to fail the controls |
| F-0034 | **The phase-status parser decided acceptance by prose substring search, and could report an unaccepted phase as accepted.** `PhaseStatus.is_accepted` returned `"ACCEPTED" in status_text.upper() and "NOT ACCEPTED" not in status_text.upper()`. Two conjoined mistakes: the search ran over the whole free-text cell, and acceptance was inferred from the *absence* of a negation rather than from an affirmative declaration. Any explanatory prose containing the token therefore accepted the phase — "Prerequisites Phases 5 and 6 are accepted" on **Phase 7's own row** made Phase 7 accepted, as did quoting `MACHINE-ACCEPTED` as history, as did writing `NOT_ACCEPTED` with an underscore. This is a **fail-open in the acceptance path**: `checker.check_prerequisites` reads the same property, so a phase that was never implemented could satisfy a later phase's prerequisite check. Same mechanism as F-0025 (governance parser deciding state by substring); same consequence class as F-0024 (acceptance asserted without being earned), which is why the severity follows F-0024 rather than F-0025. Discovered during Phase 6 post-acceptance recording and worked around by wording; the trap was already documented in F-0029's record and is now repaired rather than avoided | HIGH | CLOSED | acceptance.engine | resolved: acceptance is read from a **declared** state. `parse_declared_state` takes only the leading segment of the cell — the bold run every live row already uses — splits it into a primary state and an optional qualifier, and matches the primary against the canonical vocabulary `DeclaredPhaseState`. Only `ACCEPTED` and `MACHINE-ACCEPTED` grant acceptance, so absence of a negation can no longer accept anything. A qualifier may narrow a state but never reverse it: an accepting head carrying a negation, or a non-accepting head carrying a bare acceptance token, is **refused** as ambiguous, as is an unknown or empty state — the `findings.py` shape from F-0025. `is_locked` no longer reads `LOCKED` out of `UNLOCKED`, and `check_handoff.py`'s unlockedness comes from the same declared state rather than a second prose search. Backward compatibility proven over every live row: no phase changed meaning. 37 controls in `test_phase_status_parser.py`, none naming a phase number; 8 mutations injected and all 8 caught |
| F-0035 | **Blank lines split this findings table, and every row below the first fragment was invisible to the acceptance gate.** `findings._collect_tables` ends a table at a blank line and treats the next row as a new header, so a data row became a header whose cells are prose — `declares_id` was false and `is_finding_table` refused the fragment. Four blank lines had accumulated inside the internal blockers table, hiding **F-0027 … F-0034** from `stopping_findings` entirely. Every hidden row happened to be CLOSED, so no false PASS was ever produced; but the first OPEN HIGH written into the natural place — F-0034, above — was silently ignored, which is how this was found. Same fail-**open** class as F-0025 and the same control, reached through document layout rather than through the parser. Severity MEDIUM follows F-0025, whose blast radius is likewise finding *visibility* rather than the acceptance decision itself | MEDIUM | CLOSED | acceptance.engine | resolved: the four blank lines were removed, so every finding row sits under the one header again and all thirteen rows are visible to `stopping_findings`. No row's content was altered — this is layout, not a rewrite of recorded history. A permanent control derives the subject from the document rather than listing it: any line shaped like a finding row must appear in `parse_findings`, so the next blank line that hides one fails the suite. `findings.py` was deliberately **not** changed: its table detection is Protected Core and correct for a well-formed document, and the defect was the document's layout |

Internal BLOCKER = 0, internal HIGH = 0. F-0015 was resolved by governance erratum ERR-001; F-0024 and F-0025 by the ERR-004 remediation.
